entities.summary: In economics, the Jevons paradox, or Jevons effect, is said to occur when technological improvements that increase the efficiency of a resource's use lead to a rise, rather than a fall, in total consumption of that resource. Greater efficiency reduces the amount of the resource needed per application, lowering its effective cost; if demand is sufficiently price elastic, this induces demand such that the per-unit savings are more than offset. This results in efficiency gains in the use of resources frequently increasing, rather than decreasing, total resource consumption.
